instikit: Schools buy a licence, from $49 to $5,000, for classes, fees, and payroll. Razorpay shows $105,130 all-time and $299 in the last 30 days. There is no subscription, because the sale is a licence.
barn2-media: Shop owners pay each year for one of 19 WordPress and WooCommerce plugins. A June 2026 interview says about $1.6 million a year, and $10 million of plugin sales over the life of the business. Fifteen people. Self-reported.
standout-cv: Job seekers paid for a CV builder on top of an advice site. The September 2026 article says it reached $40,000 a month and was sold in April 2026 for a mid-six-figure sum. The page header says $360,000 a month. That header does not match the article. Self-reported.
leadsbridge: Advertisers paid so a Facebook lead landed in the CRM. A February 2019 interview says more than $150,000 a month, bootstrapped. ActiveProspect bought it in February 2021, and the terms were not disclosed. That monthly figure is from 2019.
scalefusion: Companies pay per phone or tablet so the device stays locked to the job. A February 2020 interview says $400,000 a month. By late 2015 they already had 120-plus customers and 50,000 devices. Those are different dates. Self-reported.
qwaiting: Banks and clinics pay so the queue is a virtual ticket instead of a paper one. An October 2021 interview says $66,000 a month, and the headline says $790,000 a year. A 2019 interview said more than 10,000 customers. Self-reported, and not current.
aplano: German shops pay for the shift plan and the punch clock. An August 2021 interview says they had passed five figures a month. A 2023 blog says $3 million a year and gives no source. That blog number is an estimate. The interview number is what the founder said.
salonist: Salons pay for the calendar, the till, and staff pay. In March 2021 the founder said he would not give a revenue figure. He did say 10,000 customers and 90-plus employees. Latka later estimated about $3.4 million a year, and said the company has not published revenue. The homepage now says 15,000-plus salons.
wpfunnels: WordPress shops pay for a funnel plugin: landing page, checkout, bump, upsell. Stripe shows $583,384 all-time and $3,368 in the last 30 days. There is no subscription line. About 10,000 users on the listing.
rent-round: Letting agents in the UK pay for landlord leads from a comparison site. A July 2020 interview says more than £5,000 a month, about a year after launch. That number is self-reported, and it is from 2020.
anonymous-dealership-software: Car dealers pay for a CRM that is certified to talk to CDK. A November 2026 Reddit post says $5,700 a month, 5 paying stores out of 6 live, and 57 users. Nothing raised. There is no product name and no site.
linguana: Agencies pay $25 to $129 a month so a Webflow or Framer site exists in more than one language, URLs included. 80 subscriptions add up to about $2,900 a month. The last 30 days are down. The listing asks $97,000.
aisle: Couples pay $19.99 a month to publish a destination-wedding site, plus 5% of what guests pay for rooms. 130 subscriptions add up to about $2,600 a month. The last 30 days are about $28,700, because of those guest payments.
jobhuntify: Job seekers pay for a search product that has been around since 2014. 213 subscriptions add up to about $2,000 a month. The all-time total is about $250,000. The listing also talks about free calculators, which is a different pitch.
thecontentcook: Coaches pay so a recipe book already exists and they can put their name on it. The connection is Polar, and Stripe is in the same sync. 28 subscriptions add up to about $391 a month. The last 30 days are about $1,800. The listing asks $80,000.
encharge: Software companies pay so an email goes out when billing or the product does something. A 2019 interview has $4,000 of pre-orders. A lifetime deal is described as nearly $1 million in a month. Starter Story estimates about $35,000 a month as of January 2024. That estimate is not the founder's number. A sale is mentioned, with no buyer and no price.
figmentor: Agencies pay $9 to $49 a month so a Figma frame becomes an Elementor template. The connection is Paddle, not Stripe. 137 subscriptions add up to about $1,800 a month, and that line is down. The listing asks $42,500.
swokei: Web agencies pay so a cold email already knows what is wrong with the prospect's site. The founder says $40,000 a month, and a small team. That number is self-reported, from a Reddit post on 3 November 2026.
anonymous-spain-relocation-service: People moving to Spain pay €199 to €3,000 for the visa and residency paperwork. Stripe shows about $1,200 in the last 30 days. The subscription line is only $78.45, because most fees are one-off. The listing asks $45,000. There is no product site.
anonymous-bot: A workplace pays $50 or $100 a month so a Slack message can be posted without a name. 11 subscriptions add up to about $891 a month. It has been running since 2020. The listing asks $100,000.
phonilab: French phone-repair shops pay $45 or $65 a month for certified checkout and the Qualirépar claim. Stripe shows $7,515 all-time and nothing in the last 12 months. There is no subscription line, so current revenue is unknown.
anonymous-french-automotive-saas: Garages in France pay for business software the listing will not name. Stripe now shows about $10,300 a month from 146 subscriptions, down from about $12,000 and 161 subscriptions on 8 October. The listing still asks $500,000. There is no product site.
saasant: Accounting firms pay so a spreadsheet of thousands of rows will go into QuickBooks or Xero, with an undo. GetLatka's September 2025 estimate is about $4.7 million a year. The company says 20,000+ firms. LinkedIn says 25,000+.
link-my-books: Accountants pay so Amazon, eBay, and Shopify payouts land in Xero or QuickBooks as one clean entry. GetLatka's September 2025 estimate is about $660,000 a year, with 6 people. A2X, which does the same job, has a July 2025 estimate of about $7.3 million a year.
fieldflo: Demolition and asbestos crews pay for job tracking, crew certificates, and the compliance file. A June 2026 interview says 470 customers and about $14,000 a year per customer. Latka's multiplied run rate is about $6.5 million. The founder said the real number is lower because of discounts.
zenmaid: Cleaning companies pay $49 to start, plus $9 per cleaner a month, for the schedule and the reminders. A December 2021 interview says $1.5 million a year. That number is from then.
financial-cents: Small accounting firms pay so someone can see who is closing which client's month. A November 2020 post says $8,000 a month on an accrual basis, and more cash because most firms paid annually. A later post says multi-millions, with no precise total. GetLatka lists 1,000 customers as of October 2024.
parting-pro: Funeral homes pay so a family can plan and pay online. A talk covering late 2023 says the business grew past $2 million without a normal venture round. Founderpath lists $2.5 million, with no date. Those are two figures.
towbook: Towing companies pay for dispatch, the impound lot, and the driver app. GetLatka estimates about $2.9 million a year as of October 2024, about $1.4 million in December 2023, and $839,000 in April 2021 with no source written down.
themailsupply: Cold-email shops pay about $5 a mailbox each month. Stripe, synced 5 November 2026, shows $617 a month from 8 subscriptions, and $375,327 all-time. The seller says 2024 sales were over $250,000. The listing asks $240,000. The site would not connect when this was checked.
linkody: SEO agencies pay so they can show a client the backlinks are still there. A December 2020 interview says about $140,000 a year, and the page headline says $145,000 a year. Solo. That number is from then.
anonymous-hotel-booking-for-business-tra: Trade-show and business travellers pay a one-night deposit, then the rest before check-in. Stripe, synced 5 November 2026, shows $17,218 in the last 30 days and no subscription. There is no company name and no site.
eworkorders: Factories and retail chains pay for work orders and preventive maintenance. A Latka interview on 11 August 2026 says they crossed $3 million ARR the day before the recording, with 300 customers and a team of 9. Still owned by Jeff and Brian Roscher. Bootstrapped.
limble-cmms: Larger plants pay for the same maintenance job, further upmarket. Limble's own LinkedIn post, around 4 August 2026, says $50 million ARR. A 2020 interview put it near $160,000 a month and 470 customers, while it was still mostly bootstrapped. GetLatka lists a 2023 round at a $450 million valuation.
repairdesk: Phone-repair shops pay for the ticket, the parts, and the till. Failory in October 2020 headlines $100,000 a month. A 2025 note from the COO says ARR moved from $2.7 million to $4.5 million. GetLatka's October 2024 estimate is about $2.1 million a year. Those are not the same figure.
verito: Tax and accounting firms pay for a private cloud that keeps Drake and the rest of the desktop tax stack online. The about page, checked 6 November 2026, says 1,000+ firms and 100% uptime since 2016. Prospeo estimates about $2.4 million a year. That estimate is not the company's number. No screenshot. The site blocked the check.
softledger: Mid-sized companies pay for a cloud ledger after QuickBooks and before NetSuite prices. Starter Story, 9 February 2025, says $23,100 a month. GetLatka estimates about $277,300 a year, which is close to twelve times that month, and they are still two sources. The site says 2,000+ organizations.
binderr: Accounting and law firms pay for client onboarding and the anti-money-laundering file. A June 2024 interview says about $10,000 a month then, with a typical contract around €20,000 a year. The €1.5 million and €5 million lines in that interview are targets, not results.
subbase: Construction subcontractors pay so a supplier invoice matches the purchase order. Starter Story, 22 February 2025, says $50,000 a month, about $600,000 a year, and profitable. The same write-up says they raised a $4 million seed and another $5 million.
leal: Retailers in Latin America pay so the till they already have can run a loyalty message. A June 2026 interview says 700 merchants, about $2,000 a month each, and the founder confirmed that arithmetic only directionally. They passed $5 million ARR in 2024 and he said they were north of that. The team went from 200 people to 38.
jobnimbus: Roofing contractors pay for the lead, the photos, the materials, and the invoice in one job file. GetLatka estimates about $25 million a year as of June 2024. The company has not published that figure. The homepage says 8,000+ roofing businesses, which is a customer count, not revenue.
acculynx: Roofing contractors pay for estimates, production, and the job file. GetLatka estimates about $14.4 million a year as of October 2024, with 154 employees listed on that page. That revenue figure is the estimate, not a number the company published. Founded 2008. Same lane as JobNimbus.
barbrain: Bars, restaurants, and hotels in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland pay about €52 to €99 per venue a month to count stock on a phone. An Indie Hackers post says €50,000 a month, 1,000+ businesses, and a team of about 10. The homepage also says 1,000+ venues. The post's date is not in this brief.
kassenmeister: German shops pay for a till that includes the certified security module the KassenSichV rules require. Stripe's last sync is 26 November 2025, and the key has expired. That sync shows about $10,825 in the last 30 days then, and about $215,000 all-time. It is not a live November 2026 reading.
ecrs: Independent grocers pay for the till and the back office. A September 2018 interview says about $30 million a year, about 4,000 customers, and 2 to 3 percent annual churn. The write-up came out in April 2026. No newer figure turned up. Started with $7,000 in 1989. No outside capital.
lawmatics: Law firms pay per seat so a new lead does not disappear. A January 2026 interview says more than $1 million a month, about 2,000 firms, and an average contract around $5,000. Latka also lists $12.6 million a year as of December 2025, with no source on that line. They raised $7.5 million.
agilence: Big retailers pay to find theft, fraud, and waste in till data. An August 2023 interview says $35 million in revenue, about 300 customers, and an average contract around $125,000. The write-up says the company was sold later. Hawkins calls that sale a mistake. The buyer and the price are not in the note.
revv: Body shops pay so the insurer gets proof that a car's driver-assistance sensors were calibrated. A May 2026 write-up says about $12 million a year, after breaking $10 million in 2025. About 1,000 paying customers. A separate interview counts 5,000 or more customers and 300,000 repairs. Those counts are not the same thing. They raised $33.3 million.
evotix: Companies pay for workplace health and safety software. Matt Ellison bought it in 2011 for $1, with an $11 million lawsuit attached. In January 2023 he said $17 million a year. Latka lists $47 million in December 2024 next to a combination with SAI360. Those are not the same figure.
synder: Bookkeepers pay so Stripe, PayPal, and Shopify payouts land as a clean entry in QuickBooks or Xero. GetLatka estimates about $3.8 million a year as of October 2024, up from an estimate of about $2.7 million in December 2023. The company has not published revenue. About 20,000 customers. $2 million raised in 2021.
webgility: Shops on Amazon, Shopify, eBay, and Walmart pay so orders, fees, and stock land in QuickBooks. GetLatka has three estimates that do not match: about $15.4 million in December 2023, about $22.5 million in October 2024, and about $35 million in November 2024. The company has not published revenue. About 5,000 customers. Last funding round was 2017.
order-time: Small distributors pay for stock, orders, and purchasing on top of QuickBooks. GetLatka estimates about $220,000 a year as of July 2025. The company has not published revenue. That month, two people list Order Time as their employer on LinkedIn. Founded 2016, on Latka's page.
stocksmith: People who make candles, soap, and cosmetics pay so each batch has a cost. The product was Craftybase and is now Stocksmith. GetLatka estimates about $660,000 a year as of September 2025. The company has not published revenue. LinkedIn lists 6 employees. Founded 2011 in Newcastle, Australia.
docparser: Companies pay so the same invoice or purchase-order PDF gets turned into fields they can send on. GetLatka estimates about $880,000 a year as of July 2025. The company has not published revenue. LinkedIn lists 8 employees. Latka says it was acquired. The buyer, the date, and the price are not on the record.
spectora: Home inspectors pay for the report, the schedule, and the payment. Kevin Wagstaff says it grew to $10 million a year, then roughly $30 million in 2025, and he expects $40 million by the end of 2026. That last number is what he expects, not a result. He sold half his stake in 2023 at a $90 million valuation, and another 10 percent in 2024 at $110 million. GetLatka still estimates about $5.9 million, which is not his figure.
skimmer: Pool cleaners pay for the route, the chemical log, and the recurring bill. The company says nearly 7,000 customers and more than 900,000 pools. GetLatka estimates about $5.7 million a year as of September 2025. The customer count is theirs. The yearly figure is an estimate.
gorilladesk: Pest control companies pay for the schedule and the chemical record. GetLatka estimates about $880,000 a year as of September 2025, with 8 employees. A LinkedIn-derived profile says $5 million. Those guesses conflict. A note says 3,100 or more customers and bootstrapped. One review says 11 people and profitable. Latka's headcount does not match that review.
gingr: Dog daycares and boarding kennels pay for booking, vaccine records, and check-in. GetLatka estimates about $5.5 million a year as of September 2025, with 50 employees. The company has not published that number.
planning-center: Churches pay for the Sunday plan, the volunteers, check-in, and giving. The company says 78,000 active churches and 4 million active users. More than $34 billion has passed through the giving tool. That is not their revenue. They have not published revenue. RocketReach guesses about $19.4 million a year in 2026.
method-crm: Sales teams pay for a contact list that stays in sync with QuickBooks or Xero. GetLatka lists $5.1 million a year as of August 2020, and the source for that line is not recorded. They raised $8 million. A later summary says revenue doubled over three years and does not give the new amount. 18,000+ users.
liveflow: Accountants pay so QuickBooks, bank, and revenue numbers land in a spreadsheet that refreshes. Growjo estimates about $6.7 million a year as of September 2025, with 52 employees, and GetLatka shows that estimate too. The company has not published revenue. Founded 2021. Not bootstrapped.
jetpack-workflow: Small accounting firms pay so recurring jobs and deadlines are not an Excel file. GetLatka lists $852,200 a year as of April 2021, with no source recorded, and a later estimate of about $818,100 as of October 2023. About 6,000 customers. Headcount went from 16 to 9. The $109.4 million on that page is Karbon, not Jetpack.
qqube: Controllers still on QuickBooks Desktop pay for ready-made reports. No revenue figure was published. The price is $550 the first year and $195 a year after that for one person, up to $1,950 and $685 for a ten-person licence. Extra companies are add-ons, up to $995.
ignition: Accounting firms pay so the engagement letter turns into a bill that collects itself. The CEO confirmed $30 million a year in October 2023, up from $27 million in November 2022, and $24 million in 2021. More than $1 billion of client payments passed through. That billion is not their revenue. GetLatka estimates about $46.7 million as of October 2024. The site now says more than 8,500 businesses.
acctivate: Distributors pay for inventory, the warehouse, and orders on top of QuickBooks. It has been around since 1985. GetLatka estimates about $5.6 million a year as of June 2024, with 30 employees. The company has not published revenue. A GetLatka customer count looked wrong, so it is not in the note. Fishbowl, a competitor on that site, is estimated at about $4.6 million with 225 employees. That is not Acctivate's number.
reach-reporting: Bookkeepers and fractional CFOs pay so the monthly client report is a template instead of a fresh spreadsheet. GetLatka estimates about $2.1 million a year as of September 2025, with 19 employees. Founded 2015. The company has not published revenue.
arbostar: Tree crews pay for the estimate, the schedule, and the invoice. GetLatka estimates about $10.1 million a year as of November 2024, up from about $6.2 million in December 2023. An April 2021 reading of $1.7 million has no source. Headcount went from 36 to 47. The site says more than 10,000 arborists. Those yearly figures are estimates.
knowify: Trade contractors pay for bids, job cost, and progress invoices on top of QuickBooks. GetLatka estimates about $6 million a year as of June 2024, up from a $1.3 million reading in August 2020 with no source. 19 employees. $9.1 million raised. The company says the price starts at $99 a month. That price is not the estimate.
dockwa: Marinas pay for the software, and boaters pay to book a slip. Growjo, shown on GetLatka, estimates about $5.5 million a year as of September 2025, with 47 employees. Founded 2014. The company has not published revenue. No photo today. The site asked for a security check.
commerce7: Wineries pay for the club, the tasting-room till, and the online shop. GetLatka estimates about $3.5 million a year as of September 2025, with 32 employees. Founded 2018. The company has not published revenue. The homepage says more than 3,500 wineries. The page description says more than 3,000. Both stay.
mobile-tech-rx: Mobile auto techs pay so a dealer visit full of small jobs becomes invoices tied to each car. GetLatka estimates about $1.4 million a year as of June 2025, with 13 employees. Founded 2015. Eric Garves is the CEO. The company has not published revenue.
tixian: Small promoters pay when a ticket sells. Stripe on 10 November 2026 shows $1,483 in the last 30 days and $150,205 all-time. There is no subscription line, because the money is per ticket. The listing says about 2,000 people use it. Plans are listed at $29, $99, and $299 a month. Those prices are not the Stripe total. Founded March 2024.
catalogohoy: Small shops in Latin America pay for a catalog link, orders, stock, and a till. RevenueCat on 10 November 2026 shows $399 a month from 26 subscriptions. The last 30 days were $2,040. All-time $6,293. The listing says about 5,000 people use it, one person built it, and he is selling. The asking price is $70,000. Founded March 2026.
workiz: Locksmiths, plumbers, and HVAC shops pay for the schedule, the invoice, and the payment. GetLatka estimates about $29.8 million a year as of October 2024, up from about $13.7 million in November 2023. Earlier readings run from $3.2 million in 2020 to $13.5 million in 2022. They raised $60.3 million. The press page says more than 120,000 professionals. A job ad talks about accounts of $6,000 to $15,000 a year. That is not the company's revenue.
zynk: Shops pay so orders stop being retyped into Sage. GetLatka estimates about $1.3 million a year as of December 2023, up from $1.1 million in April 2021, with 18 staff. A LinkedIn post says more than 700 businesses. An older pack said more than 500 customers and more than 100 resellers. Those counts are different dates. Sage founder Graham Wylie backed it in 2010.
anonymous-shopify-shipping-discount-app: Someone pays $9.90 a month for a Shopify app that only does shipping discounts. The listing does not name the app. Shopify on 12 November 2026 shows $7,762 in the last 30 days and $63,927 all-time. About 1,200 people, one person, bootstrapped. Founded January 2024. No public homepage on this page.
spotlight-reporting: Accounting firms pay for reports, forecasts, and dashboards they send to clients. GetLatka estimates about $10.7 million a year as of October 2024, up from $4.9 million in August 2020 and about $7.1 million in December 2023. A $3.6 million round in 2016. 52 employees. The company has not published revenue. The firm is in Wellington, New Zealand. GetLatka's page says Connecticut.
jirav: Accounting firms and fractional CFOs pay for budgets and rolling forecasts they run for many clients. GetLatka estimates about $10.9 million a year as of October 2024, up from $4.2 million in April 2021 and about $6.2 million in October 2023. $12.3 million raised. 67 employees. The company has not published revenue.
smartmoving: Moving companies pay for the estimate, the crew, and the invoice in one place. A LeadIQ figure on GetLatka estimates about $3.8 million a year as of November 2024, up from about $2.3 million in December 2023. They raised $220,000 in 2019. 46 employees. The homepage says thousands of movers. In October 2025 the founder called it the strongest year so far, which is not a revenue figure. Case studies quote the customers' own revenue, from $800,000 to $60 million, not SmartMoving's.
shop-ware: Independent garages pay for the repair order, the inspection, and the parts. GetLatka estimates about $9.9 million a year as of September 2025, with 90 employees. The company has not published revenue. Same lane as Tekmetric.
fieldpulse: HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and septic contractors pay for the schedule, the estimate, and the invoice. GetLatka estimates about $10.6 million a year as of November 2024. Growjo had $6.8 million in December 2023. An earlier reading was $9.3 million in September 2021. Those three do not line up, so they stay separate. $8.2 million raised. 87 employees.
rentvine: Property managers pay, per rented unit, for trust accounting, owner statements, maintenance, and leasing. GetLatka estimates about $5.8 million a year as of September 2025, with 53 employees. Founded 2019. The company has not published revenue.
hostfully: Short-term rental managers pay for bookings, channel management, and owner accounting, plus a guest guidebook. VentureScout says $5.5 million of revenue in 2023, up 68 percent on the year before. The about page says 40,000 clients implemented. A GetLatka page that had a higher estimate now returns not found, so that number is not here.
a2x: Bookkeepers pay so an Amazon or Shopify payout becomes one journal entry in Xero or QuickBooks. GetLatka estimates about $7.3 million a year for 2025, with 66 employees. The 5 November note on Link My Books already had that estimate, dated July 2025. A March 2026 page says more than 12,000 customers. A Misen case study is about that brand's bookkeeping cost, not A2X's revenue.
bookkeep: Shops and restaurants pay so the day's sales become one accrual entry in the books, matched to the bank deposit. Growjo, on GetLatka, estimates about $4.4 million a year as of December 2023, with 38 employees. The company has not published revenue. Plans are $19, $49, $99, $199, and $499 a month, plus 35 cents for each old entry posted later. Those are prices, not the estimate.
lmn: Landscapers pay for estimates, job cost, crew time, and invoices. GetLatka estimates about $11.6 million a year as of December 2025, with 105 employees. The company has not published revenue. An older interview says 5,000 companies and 55,000 people using it. A later post says more than 250,000 people. Bradley's own landscaping company was described as more than $10 million. That is not LMN's revenue. The product now sits on Granum.
roofr: Roofers pay for an aerial measurement, then the estimate, the proposal, and the materials order. jobber: Home-service crews pay for quotes, scheduling, invoices, and payments. GetLatka shows a reported $100 million a year in December 2022, up from $50 million in 2021. That is not a 2026 revenue reading. A May 2026 release says more than 100,000 customers and more than 400,000 service pros. It also says those customers have delivered more than $100 billion of services. That hundred billion is their work, not Jobber's revenue.
companycam: Contractors pay for a camera that keeps the project, the place, and the time on every photo. GetLatka shows an estimate of about $68 million a year as of November 2024, up from about $32 million in 2023. The company has not published revenue. An August 2025 round was reported at a $2 billion valuation. The valuation is not revenue. Lincoln, Nebraska.
housecall-pro: Plumbers, HVAC techs, electricians, and cleaners pay for scheduling, dispatch, invoices, and payments. GetLatka shows $37.2 million a year as of September 2021, with 20,000 customers then. That is a 2021 reading. They raised $175 million, including $125 million in June 2022. No newer revenue figure is in this note. No photo. Same lane as Workiz and Jobber.
hostaway: Short-term rental managers pay per listing for the channel sync, the guest inbox, and the owner statement. Growjo, on GetLatka, estimates about $23.8 million a year as of September 2025, with 216 employees. The company has not published revenue. In December 2024 they raised $365 million at a $925 million valuation. The valuation is not revenue. Portfolios they talk about run from 10 units to 8,000.
